document.title: Ambassador Dean Cable, "Subject: Afghanistan"
document.authors: Ambassador John Gunther Dean, U.S. Embassy New Delhi
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), A New Phase in the Great Game: U.S., Soviets, India, Pakistan vied to shape a new Afghanistan in late 1980s | National Security Archive
document.note: Dean summarizes Foreign Secretary Venkateswaran's briefing on the Gandhi-Gorbachev discussion of Afghanistan. Soviets seemed willing to withdraw in 1.5-2 years; Indians suspect elements in Pakistan don't want a solution because of U.S. aid. Dean suggests using India's good offices.

persons.name: John Gunther Dean
persons.role: U.S. Ambassador to India, author of cable

mentions.quote: VENKATESWARAN CALLED ME IN TO BRIEF ME ON THE GANDHI/GORBACHEV DISCUSSIONS ON AFGHANISTAN
I HAD PASSED A COPY OF PRESIDENT REAGAN'S LETTER TO HIM ON NOVEMBER 23
ON TUESDAY, DECEMBER 9 FOREIGN SECRETARY VENKATESWARAN CALLED ME IN TO BRIEF ME
WHEN HE VISITS UNDER SECRETARY ARMACOST IN WASHINGTON JANUARY 9
PRIME MINISTER GANDHI CONVEYED THE GIST OF PRESIDENT REAGAN'S LETTER TO GORBACHEV
GORBACHEV WANTS TO GET OUT OF THE AFGHANISTAN IMBROGLIO
WHEN HE VISITS UNDER SECRETARY ARMACOST IN WASHINGTON JANUARY 9

events.description: Venkateswaran briefed Ambassador Dean on Gandhi/Gorbachev discussions on Afghanistan

Indo-Soviet joint statement referring to Afghanistan
Gandhi and Gorbachev discussed Afghanistan alone with interpreters; Gandhi conveyed Reagan's letter

Ambassador Dean passed a copy of President Reagan's letter to Foreign Secretary Venkateswaran.
Indo-Soviet joint statement issued, with a portion apparently on Afghanistan.

relationships.quote: PRIME MINISTER GANDHI CONVEYED THE GIST OF PRESIDENT REAGAN'S LETTER TO GORBACHEV.

relationships.detail: Dean is the ambassador sending the cable from the embassy.
relationships.quote: ONWMEMBASSY NEW DELHI

relationships.detail: Dean sends the outgoing telegram to the State Department.
relationships.quote: DEPARTMENT OF STATE OUTGOING TELEGRAM

relationships.detail: Venkateswaran is India's Foreign Secretary.
relationships.quote: FOREIGN SECRETARY VENKATESWARAN

relationships.detail: Gorbachev is described as the Soviet leader.
relationships.quote: THE SOVIET LEADER ALLEGEDLY SAID THAT

relationships.detail: Gandhi is Prime Minister of India.
relationships.quote: PRIME MINISTER GANDHI

relationships.detail: Soviet troops are present in Afghanistan and Gorbachev reportedly wants to withdraw from it.
relationships.quote: GORBACHEV "WANTS TO GET OUT OF THE AFGHANISTAN IMBROGLIO

relationships.detail: Gorbachev wants a neutral, non-aligned Afghanistan not unfriendly to the USSR.
relationships.quote: NEUTRAL AND NON-ALIGNED AFGHANISTAN WHICH WOULD NOT BE UNFRIENDLY TO THE SOVIET UNION

relationships.detail: Indians perceived the US position as not conducive to Soviet withdrawal; the US and Soviets have differences over a settlement.
relationships.quote: PERCEIVED THE U.S. POSITION AS NOT BEING CONDUCIVE TO SOVIET WITHDRAWAL.

relationships.detail: The Soviets envisage mutual U.S. and Russian guarantees for a settlement.
relationships.quote: SOVIETS APPARENTLY WERE THINKING OF U.S. AND RUSSIAN GUARANTEES.

relationships.detail: The U.S. side suggested a three-month troop withdrawal timeframe, which the Soviets found unrealistic.
relationships.quote: THE SUGGESTION BY OUR SIDE OF THREE MONTHS WAS UNREALISTIC

relationships.detail: Venkateswaran held talks in Moscow and Delhi with senior Soviet officials.
relationships.quote: ON THE BASIS OF HIS TALKS IN MOSCOW AND DELHI WITH SENIOR SOVIET OFFICIALS

relationships.detail: Indians suspect elements in Pakistan don't want an early political solution because the Afghan problem explains U.S. assistance to Pakistan.
relationships.quote: CERTAIN ELEMENTS IN PAKISTAN DON'T REALLY WISH TO SEE AN EARLY POLITICAL SOLUTION TO THE AFGHAN PROBLEM

relationships.detail: Pakistan receives sizeable U.S. assistance.
relationships.quote: EXPLAINS THE SIZEABLE U.S. ASSISTANCE TO PAKISTAN.

relationships.detail: Dean disabused Venkateswaran of the suspicion about Pakistan and U.S. assistance.
relationships.quote: I DISABUSED HIM OF THIS FALLACY.

relationships.detail: An Indo-Soviet joint statement of Nov 28 touched on Afghanistan; the U.S. worried it implied identical views.
relationships.quote: INDO-SOVIET JOINT STATEMENT OF NOVEMBER 28 APPARENTLY REFERRING TO AFGHANISTAN SEEMS TO IMPLY AN IDENTITY OF INDIAN AND SOVIET VIEWS

relationships.detail: India's consistent position opposes Soviet troop intervention in Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: OPPOSE BOTH FOREIGN INTERVENTION (SOVIET TROOPS)

relationships.detail: India also opposes U.S. arms aid to the Afghan freedom fighters as interference.
relationships.quote: FOREIGN INTERFERENCE (U.S. ARMS AID TO THE FREEDOM FIGHTERS) IN AFGHANISTAN

relationships.detail: The U.S. provides arms aid to the freedom fighters.
relationships.quote: U.S. ARMS AID TO THE FREEDOM FIGHTERS

relationships.detail: Armacost is Under Secretary.
relationships.quote: UNDER SECRETARY ARMACOST

relationships.detail: Armacost is based in Washington.
relationships.quote: UNDER SECRETARY ARMACOST IN WASHINGTON

relationships.detail: Dean is stationed at Embassy New Delhi.
relationships.quote: EMBASSY NEW DELHI

key_claims: Gorbachev wants out of Afghanistan but wants a neutral, non-aligned government not unfriendly to the USSR.
The Soviets consider a three-month withdrawal timeframe unrealistic, and Venkateswaran thought 1.5 to 2 years could be acceptable.
India suspects elements in Pakistan do not want an early political solution because of the U.S. aid to Pakistan.
India opposes both Soviet intervention and U.S. arms aid to the freedom fighters.
Dean judges India will not do more than convey the President's letter unless convinced the U.S. is serious about enlisting its good offices.
